== Biography ==
==Birth==
John Reid was born in Edinburgh, Scotland the son of William Reid.<ref>Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Births and Baptisms. https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-births-baptisms  Accessed 3 September 2024. Note that FreeReg.uk does not have Midlothian births transcribed as of this date.</ref> Two baptismal records were found in Scotland's People for John Reid as son of William: on 4 March 1598 and on 17 October 1602, recorded in Edinburgh Parish (St. Giles Cathedral). No mothers were given in his birth record, so it is unclear at this time which one is for John Reid who married Helen Henderson. They were direct relations of William Reid who married Janet Cochrane on 10 October 1599. This William was considered a merchant elite.<ref>Brown, James J. THE SOCIAL, POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC INFLUENCES OF THE EDINBURGH MERCHANT ELITE, 1600-1638 https://era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/6860  Vol. 2, p. 516. Accessed 3 September 2024.</ref> He traded with James Cochrane and Lawrence Henderson, both surnames also associated with the <b>Mackall</b> families in Edinburgh and the Colony of Maryland.<ref>Brown. Vol. 2, p. 455 Accessed 3 September 2024.</ref>
Patrick Cochrane was his father-in-law.<ref>Brown. Vol. 1, p. 51 Accessed 3 September 2024.</ref> William served on the Edinburgh Burgess with Mungo McCall [aka Mackall and variations].<ref>Brown. Vol. 1, p. 66 Accessed 3 September 2024.</ref>
==Residence== 
The family lived in the Lawnmarket section of the High Street, and on the northside of the High Street in what was known as Bailie Reid's Close.  It is located about 1.5 blocks west of St. Giles Cathedral, between Baxter's Close on the west and Jameson's Close on the east. Note that Lawnmarket is the part of High Street where linen (also known as lawn) was sold. The complex contained both a home and tenements as well as a shop where perhaps John and his father sold their linen. <i>The land of John Ronald lay on the north side of the High Street, in Ronald's, or Bailie Reid's Close. It was owned at one time by William and George Reid, merchants, sons of George Reid, and later by James Reid of Northbrae, burgess, son of the said William; it seems to have passed from him to Robert Bell, writer. There was a tenement on the north side of the High Street, in Jameson's Close, which was owned in succession by Matthew Jameson : Robert Jameson : John Jameson : John Cunnmgham of Robertland : <b>Wlliam Reid, merchant, and his wife Jonet Cochran</b> [my emphasis] : their son James Reid, of Northbrae, heir of his father and of his uncles <b>Thomas, Alexander, John, and George Reid</b>.</i> [my emphasis]<ref>Watson, Charles Boog. “Notes on the Names of the Closes and Wynds of Old Edinburgh” Contained in The Book of the Old Edinburgh Club, Volume 12 1923; p. 17   https://archive.org/details/bookofoldedinbur1219olde p. 17 Accessed 27 September 2024.</ref>
==Marriage==
John married Helen Henderson [aka Henryson and variations] on 20 December 1621 in Edinburgh (either Edinburgh or Canongate parishes – FreeReg.UK has both places; no parents listed).<ref>Midlothian : Edinburgh : The Parish Church : Transcript : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG https://www.freereg.org.uk  Accessed 4 September 2024.</ref>
====Children====
Their children were  all baptized in Edinburgh Parish<ref>Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Births and Baptisms. https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-births-baptisms  Accessed 3 September 2024.</ref>:
#William, 28 November 1624
#John, baptized on 5 February 1626; married Margaret <b>Mackall</b> on 27 January 1647/48 or 1648/49 (FreeReg.UK has both);<ref>Midlothian : Edinburgh : The Parish Church : Transcript : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG https://www.freereg.org.uk  Accessed 4 September 2024.</ref> he was a weaver when he lived in Edinburgh; they lived in Resurrection Hundred, Calvert County, Colony of Maryland; owned Hog Neck and Orchard Neck.<ref>Carr, Dr. Lois Green https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc5000/sc5094/003000/003466/html/sc5094-3466-01.html  Accessed 1 September 2024.</ref> Margaret was the daughter of Quintigern Mungo McCall and Isobell Cochrane, ancestors of George, James Robert and Jane Mackall Prather Smith. Margaret and John were residents in Calvert County, Colony of Maryland by 1651.<ref>Carr, Dr. Lois Green. https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc5000/sc5094/003000/003466/html/sc5094-3466-01.html  Accessed 1 September 2024.</ref> <ref>Gibb, Dr. Carson. The New Early Settlers of Maryland; MSA SC 4341: Gibb Collection, updated in 2005 https://earlysettlers.msa.maryland.gov/ . Accessed 1 September 2024.</ref> <ref>For biography of their likely son, John, see Papenfuse, Edward C., et. al.  <u>A Biographical Dictionary of the Maryland Legislature 1635</u> https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000426/html/am426--673.html  Accessed 5 September 2024.</ref>
#Alexander, 1 January 1629 [parents listed in Scotland's People as Johnne Reid and Elspeth Jamesone, but this is likely a church clerk or transcription error. No record has been transcribed by FreeReg.UK to compare.
#George, 1 January 1629, twin of Alexander 
#William, 22 January 1632 (the first William presumably died young)
#Clement, 29 September 1634
#Margaret, 25 July 1637

From the Reidbourne estate court records,<ref>Proceedings and Acts of the General Assembly, March, 1707-November, 1710; Volume 27, Page 356; Archives of Maryland Online https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000027/html/am27--356.html  Accessed 31 August 2024.</ref> <ref>Janet and Bob Wolfe Genealogy. Citing: Archives of Maryland Online, Provincial Court Land Records, Volume 721, page 39, of 39-48, MSA S552-8, TL 2 SM 22-11, [MD Archives] and Archives of Maryland Online, Provincial Court Land Records, Volume 680, page 1074, index entry citing Lib. P.L. No. 5 (17254), Deed, p. 40 and 43, [MD Archives]. https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000721/html/am721--39.html Accessed 1 September 2024.</ref> <ref>Proceedings of the Provincial Court, 1679-1680/1; Volume 200, Page 6 and following;  Archives of Maryland Online  https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000700/html/am700--6.html Accessed 20 September 2024.</ref> Alexander Reid is established as George's brother. The only baptismal records found which have both born in around the same time and place are those as listed above, even though Alexander's mother is listed as Elspeth Jamesone. It was not unusual for a church clerk to make mistakes or for transcribers of the 17th century secretarial script to make errors. To substantiate them as brothers are the family connections with the Mackall families, several of whom were known to George as they lived in St. Mary's, Calvert and Charles counties, Colony of Maryland as his neighbors.
==Occupation==
John was a weaver<ref>Midlothian : Edinburgh : The Parish Church : Transcript : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG https://www.freereg.org.uk  Accessed 4 September 2024.</ref> and admitted into the Edinburgh Burgess as son of William, also a weaver, on 10 April 1622. William (the father) had been admitted on 31 December 1606 by right "of ane auld seruand" [servant]<ref>Watson, Charles Boog, ed. Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild Brethren 1406 - 1700  Scottish Record Society, Edinburgh, 1929. pp. 417 – 418 https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso46scotuoft/scottishrecordso46scotuoft/ Accessed 27 September 2024.</ref>
==Death==
There are several possible burial records listed in Scotland's People and FreeReg.uk for men named John Reid, born about 1600 and who died in Edinburgh Parish and buried in Greyfriars Kirkyard:
Scotland's People<ref>Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Deaths and Burials https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-deaths-burials Accessed 27 September 2024. Searched years between 1625 and 1680.</ref> shows 2 burials for John Reid:
*14 April 1664 Edinburgh Parish (Greyfriars Burying Ground)
*4 December 1670 Canongate Parish
*21 February 1672 Edinburgh Parish (Greyfriars Burying Ground)

According to the transcriptions done by FreeReg.uk<ref>FreeReg.uk Midlothian : Edinburgh : Greyfriars Burying Ground : Register of unspecified type : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG (https://www.freereg.org.uk/search_records/58186a5fe93790ec7524682e : viewed 29 Sep 2024) burial John Reid 22 Nov 1669.</ref>
*John Reid, a hatmaker, was buried on 27 September 1659; 
*John Reid, the son of John, a goldsmith, was buried on 14 April 1664; 
*John Reid who was buried on 22 November 1669 was a merchant; 
*John Reid, of “Markland,” was buried on 1 December 1671. 

In the Edinburgh Commissariot Court, 17 men named John Reid filed their Testament prior to 1700.<ref>Edinburgh Commissariot Records, 1601-1700. Francis J. Grant, ed. p. 231 https://archive.org/details/commissariotreco01scot/page/n5/mode/2up Accessed 27 September 2024.</ref>
Unfortunately, the information supplied in the index does not help to determine the death of John Reid of this profile. The Commissariot record for years 1701-1800 do not contain John Reid.<ref>Edinburgh Commissariot Records, 1701 -1800. Francis J. Grant, ed. https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/2632004?availability=Family%20History%20Library Accessed 27 September 2024.</ref>

Of the above it seems likely that John Reid of this profile died in 1669 and was buried on 22 November 1669 in Greyfriars Kirkyard. It may be that John became a merchant of linen after beginning his work as a weaver. Or, it may be that John was not buried in Edinburgh. One William Reid, a weaver, was buried at the east end of the kirk in Greyfriars on 24 April 1685.<ref>"Edinburgh [Scotland], Kirk of the Greyfriars, Greyfriars' Churchyard, Henry Paton, Scottish Record Society"Greyfriars Burying Ground, Edinburgh p. 541 https://archive.org/details/registerinterme00socigoog Accessed 27 September 2024.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The church which serves Edinburgh Parish is St. Giles Cathedral,<ref>St. Giles Cathedral History https://www.stgilescathedral.org.uk/history Accessed 28 September 2024.</ref> located on the High Street. Because of the lack of space for burials, the members were buried in Greyfriars Kirkyard (burying ground) beginning in 1562 with most of the interments after 1600.<ref>Greyfriars Kirkyard https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greyfriars_Kirkyard Accessed 28 September 2024.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns Johne Rait. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marione Glasgow with John Rait, tailor, on 28 June 1659.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 48; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 560; PDF pp.277 and 570; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=570 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.
